objective: Correct the canonical router/Hyper-adapter dispatch seam so Cloud IaC module-registry service assembly preserves unsupported-method semantics through the canonical path: registered path + wrong method returns 405, while truly unknown paths remain 404. No listener/deploy/cloud claim.

best_practice_sources.what_it_establishes: OpenTofu service discovery uses GET on /.well-known/terraform.json and expects JSON service identifiers such as modules.v1.
The OpenTofu module registry versions and download endpoints are GET operations under the discovered modules.v1 base.
Module source addresses can use private/custom registry hostnames; serving credentials/provider execution remain separate concerns.

alternatives_named: Register every unsupported method per route in Cloud IaC
Add path-only method mismatch detection in the router and map to 405 in the adapter
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Path-only detection preserves three-route registration, avoids capture leakage, and fixes all canonical adapter consumers consistently.
rejected_reasons: Registering every method would bloat route tables and duplicate policy per service.
Keeping 404 would preserve the direct-handler false green and degrade HTTP semantics.

findings: The router predicate returns only a boolean and does not expose captured path values, avoiding metric-label/error-detail leakage. No network, credential, or persistence path was added.
Adapter misses now scan registered templates once to distinguish 405 from 404. Current route counts are small; no I/O or allocation-heavy path was added.
Manifest, catalog, tasks, evidence, and audit rows encode local dispatch-seam scope plus explicit nonclaims.
OpenTofu module registry routes are GET-only; canonical dispatch now preserves unsupported-method semantics for those registered route shapes.
Cloud IaC manifest, HTTP/runtime catalog records, tasks/plan, tasks/todo, multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain entries were updated.
The seam improves diagnostics for future live service work by separating wrong method from unknown route before listener/deployment claims exist.
Oya VCS claim was used before source changes; no raw git/gh commands were used; no unrelated worktree changes were reverted or claimed.
Official OpenTofu docs anchor route/method expectations; repo-local evidence distinguishes local dispatch semantics from live endpoint or cloud readiness.
Explicit nonclaims exclude listener/bind/serve/deploy, auth runtime, persistence, provider execution, OpenTofu plan/apply, cloud provisioning, full verify, run-all green, and FD-001 tenant hosting.
